skill.name: Writing Hookify Rules
skill.description: Create Markdown Hookify rule files with YAML frontmatter for matching Bash, file, prompt, and workflow events.
skill.summary: Build Hookify rules that warn, block, or remind agents when configured patterns match.
skill.author: CaptainCrouton89

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences and regex examples that teach users to detect dangerous commands, eval usage, and secrets. The remaining concern is real: the skill documents dynamic command interpolation and global hidden Hookify rules, which can create cross-project command execution risk if misused.

remediation.issue: Dynamic command interpolation in rule messages
remediation.suggestion: Document this feature as advanced and risky, recommend reviewed allowlists, and warn against commands that read secrets or make network requests.

remediation.issue: Global hidden Hookify rules apply to every project
remediation.suggestion: Prefer project-local rules by default, and add guidance for auditing, listing, and removing global rules.

remediation.issue: Examples include dangerous command names without explicit context on every line
remediation.suggestion: Clarify near the examples that these strings are detection patterns, not commands to run.

content.value_statement: Teams need reliable guardrails for risky commands, file edits, and workflow reminders. This skill helps write Hookify rules with clear patterns and messages.
actual_capabilities: Explains the Markdown and YAML frontmatter structure for Hookify rule files.
Shows supported event types for Bash commands, file edits, prompts, completion checks, and task events.
Provides simple and multi-condition rule patterns using fields, operators, and regex syntax.
Gives examples for warning about dangerous commands, debug code, sensitive files, and deployment prompts.
Documents naming, storage locations, and pattern testing guidance for Hookify rule files.
limitations: It provides rule-writing guidance, not a Hookify runtime or installer.
It does not verify that generated rules are enabled in the user environment.
Regex examples may need adjustment for each project and shell environment.
Dynamic command interpolation can be risky and should be reviewed before use.

use_cases.title: Block risky shell commands
use_cases.description: Create rules that detect commands such as recursive removal, disk formatting, or unsafe permission changes before they run.

use_cases.title: Warn on sensitive file edits
use_cases.description: Build file rules that warn when edits touch environment files, credentials, certificates, or other sensitive paths.

use_cases.title: Enforce workflow reminders
use_cases.description: Add stop, prompt, or task rules that remind agents to run tests, update docs, or review deployment steps.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic rule
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner rule for one command pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Hookify rule that warns when a Bash command includes recursive removal. Include a clear message and safe alternative.

prompt_templates.title: Write a file edit warning
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a Hookify rule that warns when a file edit targets environment files and adds text that looks like an API key.

prompt_templates.title: Use multiple conditions
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Hookify rule with multiple conditions for TypeScript files that contain debug logging in the new text.

prompt_templates.title: Design a rule set
prompt_templates.prompt: Design three Hookify rules for a production release workflow: command safety, deployment prompt checks, and completion verification.

output_examples.input: Warn when a command tries to change all files to world-writable permissions.
output_examples.output: A named Bash rule that matches unsafe permission changes and shows a warning explaining safer permission choices.

output_examples.input: Remind the agent to run tests before stopping work.
output_examples.output: A stop-event rule with a concise completion checklist covering tests, build status, and documentation updates.

output_examples.input: Detect edits that add console logging to TypeScript files.
output_examples.output: A file-event rule with conditions for TypeScript paths and debug logging in the new text.

best_practices: Use narrow patterns that match the risky behavior without blocking unrelated work.
Prefer project-local rules when rules are specific to one repository.
Write messages that explain the risk and give a concrete next step.
anti_patterns: Do not use broad patterns that match common words across unrelated commands or files.
Do not put command interpolation in rule messages unless the command is trusted and reviewed.
Do not hide important rules in global locations without documenting them for the team.

faq.question: What does this skill help me create?
faq.answer: It helps create Hookify rule files that match events and show guidance when configured patterns are detected.

faq.question: Can it create rules for Bash commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains Bash event rules that match command text with regex patterns.

faq.question: Can it create rules for file edits?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers file paths, new text, old text, content fields, and multi-condition matching.

faq.question: Does it install or run Hookify?
faq.answer: No. It documents rule syntax and examples, but it does not install or execute Hookify.

faq.question: Are global rules supported?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents global and project-local rule locations, but global rules need careful review.

faq.question: Should I use dynamic command interpolation?
faq.answer: Use it only for trusted, reviewed commands because rule messages can execute local shell commands.
